Apple___Apple_scab.description: A serious fungal disease affecting apple trees, causing olive-green to black velvety spots on leaves and fruit.
Apple___Apple_scab.symptoms: Olive-green spots on leaves that turn dark brown or black. Affected leaves may yellow and drop early. Fruits develop scab-like lesions.
Apple___Apple_scab.prevention: Rake and destroy fallen leaves in autumn. Prune trees to increase airflow and sunlight penetration.
Apple___Apple_scab.biological_control: Apply preventive biological fungicides like Bacillus subtilis or copper formulations early in the season.
Apple___Apple_scab.chemical_control: Use curative fungicides such as Myclobutanil or Captan if weather is wet and cool.
Apple___Apple_scab.dosage: Captan 50 WP at 2.0g per liter of water. Apply at green tip stage.
Apple___Apple_scab.monitoring_interval: Inspect weekly during wet, cool spring weather.

Apple___Black_rot.description: Fungal pathogen that causes leaf spots (frogeye leaf spot), fruit rot, and cankers on branches.
Apple___Black_rot.symptoms: Small purple spots on leaves that enlarge to have a brown center with a purple border (frogeye). Fruit develops concentric black rings.
Apple___Black_rot.prevention: Prune out dead wood, mummified fruits, and active cankers. Destroy all pruned materials.
Apple___Black_rot.biological_control: Spray sulfur or bio-fungicides containing Bacillus amyloliquefaciens.
Apple___Black_rot.chemical_control: Apply fungicides containing Thiophanate-methyl or Captan from pink bud stage through cover sprays.
Apple___Black_rot.dosage: Thiophanate-methyl at 1.5g per liter. Observe pre-harvest interval.
Apple___Black_rot.monitoring_interval: Inspect every 7-10 days, especially after pruning or storm damage.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.description: A heteroecious rust fungus that requires both apple trees and red cedars/junipers to complete its life cycle.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.symptoms: Bright yellow-orange spots on the upper leaf surface in spring. Tube-like structures (aecia) form on the underside of leaves in summer.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.prevention: Remove nearby eastern red cedar trees if practical. Plant rust-resistant apple cultivars like Liberty or Freedom.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.biological_control: Use copper octanoate or sulfur sprays starting at bud break.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.chemical_control: Use systemic fungicides such as Myclobutanil or Triadimefon.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.dosage: Myclobutanil (Immunox) at 1.25 ml per liter of water. Spray at bud break and repeat every 7-10 days until petal fall.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.monitoring_interval: Monitor weekly from tight cluster stage through mid-summer.

Apple___healthy.description: The apple foliage is healthy with no visible signs of fungal, bacterial, or viral disease.
Apple___healthy.symptoms: Green leaves, strong petiole connection, no spots, discoloration, or deformities.
Apple___healthy.prevention: Ensure good spacing for sunlight, prune annually during dormancy, and maintain balanced irrigation.
Apple___healthy.biological_control: Not required. Maintain soil health using compost.
Apple___healthy.chemical_control: None. Avoid unnecessary pesticide applications to protect beneficial insects.
Apple___healthy.monitoring_interval: Inspect every 14 days during the active growing season.

Blueberry___healthy.description: Foliage shows excellent health with shiny, dark green leaves and strong vegetative growth.
Blueberry___healthy.symptoms: Uniform leaf color, robust shoot extension, no spotting or chlorosis.
Blueberry___healthy.prevention: Maintain soil pH between 4.5 and 5.2. Apply organic mulch and irrigate consistently.
Blueberry___healthy.biological_control: None required. Enrich soil with mycorrhizae.

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.description: A fungal disease that attacks young leaves, shoots, and fruit, forming a powdery white layer.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White, powdery patches on the undersides of leaves, causing leaves to cup upwards and distort. Young shoots may become stunted.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.prevention: Prune lower branches to improve air circulation. Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.biological_control: Apply neem oil or potassium bicarbonate mixtures.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.chemical_control: Apply sulfur-based fungicides or synthetic fungicides like Myclobutanil.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.dosage: Wettable sulfur at 4g per liter of water. Do not apply when temperatures exceed 30°C.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.monitoring_interval: Inspect every 5-7 days in warm, dry weather with high humidity.

Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.description: Cherry foliage is clean, vigorous, and free from fungal or bacterial infection.
Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.symptoms: Glossy green leaves, firm margins, no powdery coatings or shot-holes.
Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.prevention: Ensure good drainage, prune to open the canopy, and apply nitrogen fertilizer conservatively.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.description: A devastating fungal disease of corn characterized by rectangular lesions on leaf tissue.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.symptoms: Small, tan spots with yellow halos that expand into long, narrow, rectangular gray-to-tan lesions running parallel to leaf veins.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.prevention: Tillage to bury infected residue, crop rotation for at least 1-2 years, and planting resistant hybrids.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.biological_control: Utilize Trichoderma-based bio-fungicides to accelerate crop residue decomposition.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.chemical_control: Apply strobilurin or triazole fungicides (e.g., Pyraclostrobin, Propiconazole) if severe infection is forecast during tasseling.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.dosage: Propiconazole 41.8% EC at 0.5 ml per liter of water.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.monitoring_interval: Monitor twice weekly from tasseling to silking stages.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.description: Fungal infection that spreads via wind-borne spores, favored by cool temperatures and high humidity.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.symptoms: Elongated golden-brown to cinnamon-brown pustules on both upper and lower leaf surfaces. Pustules rupture to release powdery spores.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.prevention: Plant resistant corn hybrids. Manage plant population density to reduce canopy humidity.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.biological_control: Use bio-agents like Bacillus subtilis to inhibit spore germination.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.chemical_control: Fungicides containing Azoxystrobin or Pyraclostrobin are highly effective.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.dosage: Azoxystrobin 250 SC at 1.0 ml per liter. Apply at first sign of pustules.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.monitoring_interval: Inspect every 7 days during cool, humid spells.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.description: Fungal disease causing large, cigar-shaped lesions on corn leaves, leading to premature leaf death.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Long, elliptical, grayish-green or tan lesions (1-6 inches long), often beginning on lower leaves and progressing upwards.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.prevention: Rotate crops away from corn for 2 years. Destroy infected crop residue. Plant resistant hybrids.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.biological_control: Apply foliar bio-fungicides like Bacillus amyloliquefaciens.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.chemical_control: Use fungicides containing Propiconazole or Azoxystrobin.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.dosage: Propiconazole + Azoxystrobin premix at 1.2 ml per liter of water.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.monitoring_interval: Inspect every 7 days from vegetative stage V8 through grain fill.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.description: Corn leaves are dark green, upright, and display optimal photosynthetic potential.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.symptoms: Uniform deep green leaves, strong stalks, no lesions or rust pustules.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.prevention: Rotate crops with legumes. Ensure adequate nitrogen and potassium levels.

Grape___Black_rot.description: A destructive fungal disease of grapes that infects leaves, shoots, and berries, turning berries into dry black shriveled mummies.
Grape___Black_rot.symptoms: Reddish-brown circular spots on leaves with black pinpoint fruiting bodies. Grapes turn brown, shrivel, and transform into hard black mummies.
Grape___Black_rot.prevention: Remove and destroy all mummified berries from vines and ground. Keep canopy open to direct sunlight.
Grape___Black_rot.biological_control: Apply copper formulations or Bacillus subtilis during early leaf development.
Grape___Black_rot.chemical_control: Apply Mancozeb, Myclobutanil, or Captan starting at bud break.
Grape___Black_rot.dosage: Mancozeb 75 DG at 2.5g per liter. Maintain safety interval (do not apply close to harvest).
Grape___Black_rot.monitoring_interval: Monitor twice weekly from bud break through fruit set.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).description: A complex wood-decay disease of grapevines causing leaf striping, berry spotting, and vine decline.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).symptoms: Leaf tissue yellows and dries between major veins, creating a green-and-red/yellow 'tiger-stripe' pattern. Berries show tiny dark spots.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).prevention: Protect pruning wounds with wound sealant. Prune in dry weather. Remove and burn dead vines.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).biological_control: Inoculate pruning wounds with Trichoderma harzianum species to prevent colonization.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).chemical_control: No highly effective chemical cure exists for systemic vine infection; focus is on wound protection.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).dosage: Wound paste / sealant applied immediately after pruning.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).monitoring_interval: Inspect vines monthly, especially in mid-to-late summer.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.description: Fungal disease that causes spots on grape leaves, often developing late in the season.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.symptoms: Small, dull brown spots on leaves that merge into large necrotic areas, eventually causing leaf drying and premature drop.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.prevention: Rake and burn fallen leaves. Prune lower canopy leaves to reduce humidity near soil level.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.chemical_control: Apply broad-spectrum fungicides such as Copper Oxychloride or Chlorothalonil.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.dosage: Copper Oxychloride 50 WP at 3g per liter of water.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.monitoring_interval: Inspect every 14 days, accelerating as harvest approaches.

Grape___healthy.description: Grapevine leaves are fully expanded, deep green, and free from mildew, rot, or discoloration.
Grape___healthy.symptoms: Smooth, green leaves without white coatings, black spots, or necrotic margins.
Grape___healthy.prevention: Implement vertical shoot positioning (VSP) trellis systems for optimal airflow. Prune suckers regularly.
Grape___healthy.biological_control: Apply compost tea to support leaf microbiome.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).description: One of the most destructive bacterial diseases of citrus, spread by the Asian citrus psyllid vector.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).symptoms: Asymmetric yellow mottling of leaves ('blotchy mottle'), small yellow upright leaves, stunted twigs. Fruit is small, lopsided, green at the bottom, and bitter.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).prevention: Plant only certified disease-free nursery stock. Monitor for Asian citrus psyllids using yellow sticky cards.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).biological_control: Release parasitic wasps (Tamarixia radiata) to control the psyllid population. Use neem-based insecticidal soaps.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).chemical_control: No cure for the bacterium. Control the vector using systemic insecticides like Imidacloprid.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).dosage: Imidacloprid 200 SL at 0.5 ml per liter applied as soil drench around trunk.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).monitoring_interval: Check yellow sticky traps weekly; inspect foliage every 10 days.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.description: A bacterial pathogen causing leaf spotting, defoliation, and fruit blemishes on stone fruit crops.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, water-soaked, angular gray-to-brown spots on leaves. Center of spots may fall out, giving a 'shot-hole' appearance. Fruit develops dark lesions.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Avoid planting highly susceptible cultivars. Apply balanced fertilizer to keep trees vigorous.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.biological_control: Apply preventive copper sprays during bud break and leaf fall.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.chemical_control: Use Oxytetracycline (Mycoshield) during cover periods to prevent fruit damage.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.dosage: Oxytetracycline 200g per 100 liters of water. Spray at 7-10 day intervals starting at shuck split.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.monitoring_interval: Monitor weekly, especially after rain/wind storms in spring.

Peach___healthy.description: Foliage is clean and highly active. Leaves have normal lanceolate shape and uniform green color.
Peach___healthy.symptoms: No lesions, yellowing, leaf curling, or gummy exudates.
Peach___healthy.prevention: Prune in late winter. Paint trunks white to prevent sun scald and subsequent insect invasion.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.description: A serious bacterial disease of peppers causing rapid defoliation, blossom drop, and scarred fruit.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, circular, dark spots with yellow halos on leaves, which look raised on leaf undersides. Severe infections lead to leaf yellowing and drop.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Use certified pathogen-free seeds. Rotate crops with non-solanaceous plants for 2-3 years. Avoid working in wet fields.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.biological_control: Apply copper hydroxide mixed with mancozeb to increase copper availability against resistant strains.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.dosage: Copper Hydroxide 50 WP at 2.0g per liter. Spray preventatively.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.monitoring_interval: Inspect every 5 days during warm, rainy seasons.

Pepper,_bell___healthy.description: Pepper plants show robust growth, healthy green canopy, and balanced flowering.
Pepper,_bell___healthy.symptoms: Flat, green leaves, thick stems, no leaf drop or circular lesions.
Pepper,_bell___healthy.prevention: Apply mulch to keep moisture stable. Avoid overhead watering.

Potato___Early_blight.description: A common fungal disease characterized by concentric, target-like brown spots on older leaves first.
Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings (target board pattern) starting on older foliage. Leaf margin may yellow.
Potato___Early_blight.prevention: Maintain vine vigor through adequate nitrogen fertilizing. Rotate crops. Destroy post-harvest debris.
Potato___Early_blight.biological_control: Apply Bacillus subtilis or Streptomyces lydicus formulations.
Potato___Early_blight.chemical_control: Spray protective fungicides like Chlorothalonil or Mancozeb.
Potato___Early_blight.dosage: Mancozeb 75 WP at 2g per liter of water. Apply at first sign of disease.
Potato___Early_blight.monitoring_interval: Monitor every 7 days once lower leaves touch the ground.

Potato___Late_blight.description: A highly destructive oomycete disease (infamous for the Irish Potato Famine) that can wipe out fields in days under wet, cool conditions.
Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Large, irregular water-soaked spots on leaves that quickly turn brown/black. A white, fuzzy fungal growth appears on leaf undersides in high humidity.
Potato___Late_blight.prevention: Plant resistant varieties. Destroy volunteer potatoes. Avoid overhead irrigation.
Potato___Late_blight.biological_control: Apply copper fungicides or bio-fungicides containing Bacillus amyloliquefaciens.
Potato___Late_blight.chemical_control: Apply systemic or contact fungicides such as Metalaxyl-M, Azoxystrobin, or Cymoxanil.
Potato___Late_blight.dosage: Metalaxyl 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP at 2.5g per liter. Spray immediately when disease is forecast.
Potato___Late_blight.monitoring_interval: Monitor daily if cool (10-20°C) and rainy weather persists.

Potato___healthy.description: Potato vines show rich green color, thick stems, and healthy leaf development without signs of blight.
Potato___healthy.symptoms: Smooth, green leaves, no dark spots, wilted margins, or white mold.
Potato___healthy.prevention: Use certified seed tubers. Space rows to encourage quick drying of leaves.

Raspberry___healthy.description: Raspberry canes show strong growth with bright green trifoliate leaves.
Raspberry___healthy.symptoms: Green leaves, no rust, leaf spots, or stem lesions.
Raspberry___healthy.prevention: Prune out spent floricanes after harvest. Keep rows narrow to promote airflow.

Soybean___healthy.description: Soybean leaves are broad, uniform green, and exhibit excellent nodulation and health.
Soybean___healthy.symptoms: No defoliation, yellowing, mosaic patterns, or leaf rust spots.
Soybean___healthy.prevention: Inoculate seeds with Rhizobium. Practice crop rotation with corn.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.description: A fungal disease that covers squash foliage with a white, talcum-powder-like coating, reducing yields.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White powdery spots on leaves and stems. Affected leaves eventually turn yellow, brown, dry, and paper-like.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.prevention: Grow squash in full sun. Space plants properly to avoid crowding. Plant resistant varieties.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.biological_control: Spray horticultural oils, neem oil, or potassium bicarbonate solutions.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.chemical_control: Apply fungicides containing Triadimefon or Myclobutanil.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.dosage: Myclobutanil at 0.4g per liter of water. Apply at first sign and repeat in 10 days.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.description: A fungal disease that causes purple blotches on strawberry leaves, which can merge and make leaves look scorched.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.symptoms: Numerous small, purplish spots on the upper leaf surface that enlarge and become dark brown, dry, and curled at the edges.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.prevention: Remove old leaves at renovation. Avoid excess nitrogen fertilizer which stimulates soft leaves.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.biological_control: Apply copper octanoate early in spring.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.chemical_control: Use fungicides containing Captan or Thiophanate-methyl.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.dosage: Captan 50 WP at 2.0g per liter. Spray at pre-bloom and repeat post-harvest.

Strawberry___healthy.description: Strawberry runners and leaves are compact, vibrant green, and clean.
Strawberry___healthy.symptoms: Three-lobed green leaves, clean margins, no reddish spots or grey rot.
Strawberry___healthy.prevention: Mulch rows with clean straw to prevent leaf contact with soil. Clean runners.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.description: Bacterial pathogen that causes dark water-soaked spots on leaves and black spots on fruit.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, dark, circular spots on leaves, often surrounded by a yellow halo. Spots can coalesce, causing leaves to yellow and drop.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Avoid overhead watering. Practice strict sanitation of stakes and tools. Rotate crops.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.biological_control: Apply copper fungicides mixed with bio-agents like Bacillus subtilis.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.dosage: Copper Hydroxide at 2.0g per liter of water.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.monitoring_interval: Inspect every 5-7 days, especially during rainy, humid periods.

Tomato___Early_blight.description: A fungal disease that causes dark brown spots with concentric ring patterns on older leaves.
Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: Concentric target-like rings on lower leaves, progressing to yellowing and drop. Stem lesions can lead to collar rot.
Tomato___Early_blight.prevention: Stake plants. Mulch soil surface. Rotate crops out of Solanaceae family for 3 years.
Tomato___Early_blight.biological_control: Apply Trichoderma harzianum to soil; spray Bacillus amyloliquefaciens on leaves.
Tomato___Early_blight.dosage: Mancozeb 75 WP at 2.0g per liter or Chlorothalonil 75 WP at 2.0g per liter.

Tomato___Late_blight.description: A highly destructive oomycete disease causing rapid leaf browning and fruit rot under cool, damp conditions.
Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Large water-soaked lesions on leaves turning black. Fuzzy white mold under leaves in high humidity. Fruit develops firm, brown lesions.
Tomato___Late_blight.prevention: Plant resistant cultivars. Keep foliage dry. Promptly remove and destroy infected plants.
Tomato___Late_blight.biological_control: Copper hydroxide sprays or bio-fungicides containing Bacillus amyloliquefaciens.
Tomato___Late_blight.chemical_control: Use fungicides containing Cymoxanil, Metalaxyl, or Azoxystrobin.
Tomato___Late_blight.dosage: Metalaxyl-M + Mancozeb (Ridomil Gold) at 2.5g per liter. Spray early.
Tomato___Late_blight.monitoring_interval: Check daily during periods of high humidity and temperatures between 10-20°C.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.description: Fungal disease primarily affecting tomato leaves in greenhouses or high humidity fields.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.symptoms: Pale green/yellow spots on upper leaf surfaces. Olive-green to gray velvety fungal growth on leaf undersides.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.prevention: Increase greenhouse ventilation. Keep relative humidity below 85%. Plant resistant hybrids.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.chemical_control: Apply fungicides like Chlorothalonil or Azoxystrobin.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.dosage: Azoxystrobin 250 SC at 1 ml per liter of water.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.monitoring_interval: Inspect every 7 days in high humidity conditions.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.description: A destructive fungal leaf spot disease of tomatoes, causing severe defoliation and subsequent sunscald.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Numerous small, circular spots with dark brown margins and greyish-white centers on lower leaves, with tiny black specks (pycnidia) inside.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.prevention: Rotate crops. Control solanaceous weeds. Clean stakes and tools. Mulch base.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.biological_control: Use copper octanoate or Bacillus subtilis based sprays.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.chemical_control: Use fungicides containing Mancozeb, Chlorothalonil, or Copper Hydroxide.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.dosage: Chlorothalonil at 2.0g per liter. Spray every 7-10 days starting at fruit set.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.monitoring_interval: Check lower leaves twice weekly during wet summer months.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.description: Tiny arachnid pests that suck cell contents from tomato leaves, forming fine webs.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.symptoms: Yellow speckled spotting (stippling) on leaves, leaf bronzing, fine silk webbing under leaves and on stems.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.prevention: Avoid over-fertilizing with nitrogen (which promotes soft, tasty foliage). Keep plants well-irrigated.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.biological_control: Release predatory mites (Phytoseiulus persimilis). Use insecticidal soaps or neem oil.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.chemical_control: Use specific miticides/acaricides like Abamectin or Spiromesifen.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.dosage: Abamectin 1.8% EC at 0.5 ml per liter of water.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.monitoring_interval: Inspect lower leaf undersides twice weekly in hot, dry weather.

Tomato___Target_Spot.description: Fungal disease causing target-like lesions on leaves, stems, and fruit.
Tomato___Target_Spot.symptoms: Small, brown, circular spots with concentric rings on leaves and pitted dark lesions on fruit.
Tomato___Target_Spot.prevention: Prune suckers to improve airflow. Maintain crop rotation.
Tomato___Target_Spot.dosage: Chlorothalonil at 2.0g per liter of water.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.description: A devastating plant virus transmitted by whiteflies (Bemisia tabaci).
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.symptoms: Severe stunting, leaves curl upwards and inwards, leaves turn chlorotic (yellow) between veins. Flowers drop, preventing fruit set.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.prevention: Use virus-free transplants. Install fine insect mesh in greenhouses. Control weeds.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.biological_control: Release natural predators of whiteflies like lacewings or Encarsia formosa wasps. Apply neem oil.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.chemical_control: No cure for the virus. Control the whitefly vector using systemic insecticides (e.g., Acetamiprid, Imidacloprid).
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.dosage: Acetamiprid 20 SP at 0.3g per liter of water.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.monitoring_interval: Monitor whitefly populations using yellow sticky cards, checked twice weekly.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.description: A highly stable, contagious tobamovirus that spreads mechanically through hands, tools, and plant contact.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.symptoms: Light and dark green mottling (mosaic) on leaves, leaf distortion (shoestringing), stunted growth. Fruit may show internal browning.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.prevention: Wash hands with soap and water/milk before handling plants. Sanitize tools. Do not smoke near plants (tobacco can carry related viruses).
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.biological_control: None. Disinfect seeds in a 10% trisodium phosphate (TSP) solution before sowing.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.chemical_control: No chemical treatment is available for viral infections. Rougue (remove) and burn infected plants immediately.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.monitoring_interval: Check plants daily for mosaic pattern anomalies.

Tomato___healthy.description: Tomato foliage is clean, upright, and showing robust green pigmentation.
Tomato___healthy.symptoms: Deep green leaves, sturdy stems, no spots, wilting, or yellowing.
Tomato___healthy.prevention: Prune lower leaves to prevent splash-back from soil. Water at the base.
